decisions.reason: Because the mobile check-in app is closely related to the firm's airport and passenger-handling expertise and the firm has some in-house technology capability, management would likely keep it, though its software-heavy nature and limited visible evidence of continued rollout leave a moderate risk of withdrawal.

Passenger processing technology fits the firm's established integrated airport-security offer especially well, and the explicit 2019 launch suggests a committed commercial push, so absorptive capacity arguments favor keeping it despite some uncertainty about later market traction.

The self-service airline check-in solution builds on the firm's existing airport-facing services and can be learned from and improved with its operational know-how, so management would be inclined to keep it, although adjacency to airline IT systems makes it somewhat riskier than core security services.
